en: Mount Mayon erupts when immense pressure from trapped magma forces its way up through the central volcanic vent.
Lake Taal formed when massive volcanic eruptions collapsed the ground into a large crater that eventually filled with rainwater.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River carved its massive caves because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the limestone rock over millennia.
The deep Philippine Trench formed because the Philippine Sea Plate continuously subducts beneath the overriding Philippine Mobile Belt.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills formed when ancient coral reefs were uplifted by tectonic plates and subsequently shaped by rainwater erosion.
Maria Cristina Falls generates electricity because the fast-falling water spins large turbines connected to generators at the river's outlet.
Tubbataha Reef thrives because its shallow, clear, sunlit waters allow photosynthetic coral polyps to continuously build hard limestone structures.
The Sierra Madre mountain range shields eastern Luzon from typhoons because its dense forests absorb heavy rain and block strong winds.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent soil erosion because their stepped stone walls slow down rainwater runoff on the steep slopes.
Tiwi Geothermal Plant produces power because hot underground magma heats groundwater into high-pressure steam that spins surface electricity generators.
Strong ocean currents rush through the San Bernardino Strait because rising tides are squeezed through the narrow gap between islands.
Mangrove forests in the Sulu Sea stabilize coastlines because their dense, tangled roots trap sediment and absorb crashing wave energy.
